claims.claim: In the studied treatment, displaying rules increased newcomer comments and the probability of compliant comments.
claims.limitations: Does not fully distinguish participant selection from individual behaviour change.

claims.claim: Increased participation can increase the absolute number of comments removed even when compliance improves.
claims.limitations: Not a direct measure of moderator labour hours.

claims.claim: Making punishment available does not improve cooperation in every setting.
claims.limitations: Contradicts a broad claim about sanctions, not the rule-visibility intervention.

claims.claim: Volunteer enforcement also involves managing disputes and hostility.
claims.limitations: Costs are not estimated for a single intervention.

claims.claim: Debriefs show a favourable average effect relative to controls in the 2013 synthesis.
claims.limitations: Aggregate effect does not imply the same improvement for a new team.

claims.claim: A later synthesis reports a favourable aggregate effect for after-action reviews.
claims.limitations: Full methods not yet audited.

claims.claim: Some additional debrief components did not show significant incremental contribution in the 2022 synthesis.
claims.limitations: Does not establish equivalence of variants.

claims.claim: Action points retained on a Scrum board were observed in an Agile team.
claims.limitations: Supports implementation, not causal effect.

claims.claim: Observed ways of retaining retrospective actions differed across teams and accounts.
claims.limitations: One organisation; limited observation.

claims.claim: An end-of-shift debrief intervention was associated with improvements in three burnout dimensions relative to control.
claims.limitations: Full methods and duration not yet audited; not evidence for distributed care.

claims.claim: The proposed mechanism through reduced job demands was not supported in the same study.
claims.limitations: Mediation results do not provide complete causal mechanism identification.

claims.claim: Loomio documents assignment of steward and stewardee roles and responsibilities for maintaining the practice.
claims.limitations: Documents protocol without a comparator.

claims.claim: In the experimental tasks examined, gender and others' expectations were relevant to allocation of low-promotability tasks.
claims.limitations: Does not test care-work rotation; simplified monetary tasks.

claims.claim: The prospect of a penalty for refusal did not increase the gender allocation gap in the reported test.
claims.limitations: Does not rule out backlash in other settings.

claims.claim: Volunteer maintenance work can generate conflict over conditions and legitimacy of the role.
claims.limitations: Does not evaluate stewardship or rotation.

claims.claim: Explicit delegation, accountability, and information distribution are proposed responses to informal elites.
claims.limitations: Historical proposal and diagnosis, not a trial.

claims.claim: In the Wikia sample, growth is associated with indicators of concentrated authority.
claims.limitations: Oligarchy proxy; no mandate intervention.

claims.claim: The Phoenix Co-housing case documents delegated domains and organised participation.
claims.limitations: Sociocratic package; specific mandate effect not isolated.

claims.claim: Adoption of the governance package did not eliminate reported status asymmetries.
claims.limitations: Does not estimate net effect of formalisation.

claims.claim: Seeds for Change defines a consensus protocol and explicit conditions and approaches to deadlock.
claims.locator: Conditions; What if we can't agree?
claims.limitations: Protocol documentation, not comparative effectiveness evidence.

claims.claim: Sociocracy 3.0 defines a specific consent decision-making procedure.
claims.limitations: Does not justify treating every sociocratic implementation as S3.

claims.claim: Apache documents public proposal and a waiting period, normally 72 hours, for lazy consensus.
claims.limitations: Prescription; does not measure implementation frequency.

claims.claim: Phoenix Co-housing provides an observed case of consent within a broader governance system.
claims.limitations: No separate comparison with consensus or voting.

claims.claim: The same case reports tensions around objections that were difficult to resolve.
claims.limitations: Does not establish general frequency of the problem.

claims.claim: FLOSS archives document different asynchronous decision processes.
claims.limitations: External channels are not completely observable.

claims.claim: For software-change decisions, projects classified as more successful showed longer episodes but fewer messages.
claims.limitations: Does not show that slower decision episodes improve performance.

claims.claim: No identifiable decision announcement was found in 45 of 360 episodes.
claims.limitations: Decisions may have occurred in channels outside the archive.

claims.claim: The Fire project ceased development after the period studied.
claims.limitations: Exact cessation date and cause were not established in this cycle.

claims.claim: Task conflict did not show a positive average relationship with performance in the examined meta-analysis.
claims.limitations: Contradicts a general formula, not every structured dissent intervention.

claims.claim: Relationship and process conflict show more consistently negative associations, with results depending on construct and outcome.
claims.limitations: Aggregate associations; moderators are not causal interventions.

claims.claim: Authentic dissent outperformed three devil's-advocate conditions for solution quantity and quality in the reported study.
claims.limitations: Sample and full methods not yet verified.

claims.claim: An objection procedure and a relational-conflict process should remain distinct records.
claims.locator: Working Patterns decision D01; C007 synthesis
claims.limitations: Methodological synthesis, not an experimental result.
